title: ESP32-S3 SHA-512 placement A/B for fork #94, CPU at 80 MHz
board: Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 class board, ESP32-S3 rev v0.2, 8 MB flash, USB-Serial/JTAG; the board whose MAC ends 37:68

toolchain.rustc: rustc 1.97.0-nightly (8ea53bcd7 2026-07-08) (esp 1.97.0.0), xtensa-esp32s3-none-elf, opt-level 3, lto fat, codegen-units 1

harness: WS-BENCH firmware for the S3 (private copy of the student repo's firmware-s3, not published here): ChaCha20-Poly1305 seal/open, Ed25519 and SHA-512 for rind and RustCrypto/dalek. A row is the firmware's median of `iters` timed samples (32, or 8 for Ed25519).
note: Control of an interleaved A/B on one ESP32-S3. Each run is one flash of the control image; the run's value is the median over that boot's complete rounds. Every flash of every image is in ab.json.

control.what: #94 before the change: the old default, unrolled SHA-512 running from flash

rolled.what: #94 at 7cbb9a70: the rolled loop in flash, the new default

unrolled.what: #94 at 7cbb9a70 with esp32s3-sha512-unrolled and the bench-only tools/iram-bench-only-rind.diff, which puts the unrolled block in IRAM; not in the PR

results_intro: Interleaved flashes of three SHA-512 placements from fork #94 on one ESP32-S3. The tables below are the control image. [ab.md](ab.md) has every image against the control, [RUNS.md](RUNS.md) every control run, and [NOTES.md](NOTES.md) the method, the run counts and what each image is.
results_ab: [ab.md](ab.md) has every image against the control, flash by flash. Images flashed fewer than three times do not meet the three-run rule; [NOTES.md](NOTES.md) says which.
